mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the FEDFUNDS rate above 3.5% for two consecutive months reduces discount rates, lowering the present value of future earnings and pushing S&P 500 forward returns negative over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 3.5% and remains above for two consecutive months
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns show no statistically significant deviation from zero (p > 0.05) during the FEDFUNDS high phase.

mechanism_narrative: Rising monthly PAYEMS accompanied by a decline in UNRATE predicts stronger labor market absorption, boosting consumer confidence and driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases while UNRATE decreases in the same month
failure_condition: Multivariate Granger causality test rejects PAYEMS leading UNRATE in the 20-day window (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in GDPC1 (quarterly) coinciding with a surge in HOUST (monthly) indicates accelerating business and housing demand, which elevates equity valuation multiples and produces positive 5-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 exceeds prior quarter by >10% and HOUST increases by >5% in the same month
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not statistically different from zero (p > 0.05) during the signal window.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly expansion in INDPRO exceeding 5% while RSAFS falls by >2% signals supply-side imbalances favoring equities, generating positive 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: Return pattern repeats the signal but with no significant deviation from the mean (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When FEDFUNDS remains below 2% for three consecutive months, the low-rate environment suppresses risk premia, producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS stays below 2% for three consecutive months
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are positive and statistically significant (p < 0.05) during the low-rate period.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp decline in UNRATE below 4% combined with a sustained drop in PAYEMS suggests weak wage growth and labor market softening, which tends to depress consumer spending and drive negative 60-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE < 4% for two consecutive months and PAYEMS month-over-month < -3% for three months
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns show no consistent negative trend during the softening regime (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sudden spike in HOUST (monthly) followed by a 2%+ monthly increase in GDPC1 for the next two months indicates a rapid acceleration in demand, which elevates equity risk premiums and yields positive 20-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: HOUST increases by >10% in one month and GDPC1 increases by >2% in the following two months
failure_condition: 20-day returns revert to zero mean with no statistically significant deviation during the shock (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the interaction between CPIAUCSL (monthly) and FEDFUNDS (monthly) forms a counterclockwise cross in their 12-month moving patterns, it predicts a regime shift toward deflationary expectations that precedes negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 days.
candidate_trigger: 12-month moving CPIAUCSL and FEDFUNDS form a counterclockwise cross
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns remain positive and statistically significant (p < 0.05) during the regime shift.
